title: Cut six broccoli florets to short stalks with a paring knife while the other hand steadies a half head
instruction: Cut each of the six broccoli florets off the half head with a short stalk, and leave the florets and the knife on the board.
context: Food preparation workers peel and cut vegetables; BLS reports 908,500 jobs in 2025 (https://www.bls.gov/ooh/food-preparation-and-serving/food-preparation-workers.htm). O*NET 35-2021.00 lists cutting food; Purdue FoodLink describes broccoli florets. This is occupation-wide evidence. The challenge is cutting crowded stalks 10-30 mm below their first side branches under blade resistance while the other hand steadies the stem, without damaging crowns or letting the knife turn.
setup: Station table. Fixed OXO11272900 polypropylene board, 368.3 x 535.9 mm, 16 mm thick estimated, centred (290, 0) mm. One fresh lengthwise half head, representative 125 g total (a measured half mass); six representative 27/32/33/33/32/27 mm free stalks, 7 mm sample-median thickness; crowns 38/40/44/44/40/38 mm. Main stem original diameter 40 mm, length 145 mm, distal 25 mm narrowing to 32 mm, six branch origins/angles/heights and 14 g distal/41 g remaining-stem mass allocation are estimates. A starts flat-face down at (240,-30) mm, yaw 40 degrees, wholly on the board. The left gripper steadies the bare butt in a 45-degree opposed pinch; the half stays board-supported and slides between cuts. Mercer M23900P knife (76 mm maker blade; estimated 100 x 22 x 24 mm handle, 10 x 30 x 26 mm guard, 50 g mass) stands edge-down at handle centre (330,-225) mm, blade toward -x. The gripper pinches the handle 27.5 mm toward its guard, with the opposed pads exchanged for wrist reach; a small putty dab stabilizes the real rounded handle, simulated underside flat. Ruler 300 x 20 x 2 mm at (490, 0) mm. B mirrors A and exchanges arms. Two fixed layouts, zero jitter, not a distribution of heads.
scoring: Score 0 if at any time: any part of the blade comes within 30 mm of the gripper holding the stem, or touches it; the knife handle or guard touches the gripper holding the stem; a gripper crushes a crown (crushed or broken buds after the trial; in simulation over 2 mm inside a bud); a floret is torn off without a cut; pre-cut or substituted florets are used. Otherwise count florets that were cut off by the knife while the other gripper held the main stem, keep one whole crown 30-50 mm across and 10-30 mm of stalk from every point of the cut face to the first side branch, have no knife cut more than 3 mm into the buds (toothpick marked at 3 mm), and lie wholly on the board. 0 florets: 0; 1-2: 0.33; 3-5: 0.67; 6: 1.0. One or two damaged crowns cap the score at 0.67, three or more at 0.33. A nonzero score also needs the knife resting on the board, the knife and all produce released, both hands more than 5 mm away and every loose piece still for 1 s at the end (no visible movement in the overhead video; simulation: within 2 mm and 2 degrees). Tools: whole-trial video with a visible 30 mm holding-gripper mark and side-view ruler for cutting, holding and clearance; ruler on overhead and side photos of every piece for crowns and stalks; a toothpick marked at 3 mm for cuts in the buds.
reset_notes: Specimen: one ordinary supermarket broccoli head gives two trial halves ($4.29 bunch, opened retail route). Measured Nov 23 on 2 heads/4 halves with ruler, 1 g scale and stopwatch: remove leaves, halve lengthwise through the main stem, lay cut-face down in 47 and 53 s per head. Every one of the 4 halves had six attached florets with 30-50 mm crowns; free stalks 23-39 mm, thickness 5-10 mm; half masses 112-133 g. Acceptance: with the ruler, check that a firm half has six attached primary florets with crowns 30-50 mm, stalks 23-39 mm and thickness 5-10 mm; reject limp, hollow, torn or pre-cut branches and take the other half or the next head; trim small non-target branches. Scoring is judged against each floret's own first side branch, so natural branch placement changes the knife path, not the success rule. Lay the half flat, wholly on the board, bare butt clear for the opposed pinch; put knife and ruler at their marks. Putty only holds the real knife upright for a repeatable pickup and has no role in cutting. Wash and dry board and knife; use a fresh accepted half per trial; buy produce per session. Simulation writes exact poses and zero velocities, rejoins tissue joints and settles 0.5 s; start error over 4 mm/3 deg invalidates the trial.
fidelity: Rigid half head: six 27-33 mm stalks, 7 mm thick, 125 g total, within measured ranges. Stem shape, branch placement, masses and friction are estimates. Native stem grip, board-supported side cuts; no action pose writes. Loaded edge sweeps release tissue joints. Blade contacts board/robot/main stem. Branch resistance: 0.4 N/mm feed + 0.15 N/mm drag, full blade moment and equal reaction. Force is estimated; compliance, sap, fracture and changing cut faces omitted. Two fixed layouts.
scores: Dream-1: A 0.0/B 0.0 (dream-20261124T042550), step limit, no cuts. Demo: A 1.0/B 1.0 (demo-20261124T034702) with the full blade moment. Both on the same frozen task.py 07f48b93.
